content.content:
1	Equipment is frequently attached to the outside of a pipe after the pipe has been installed. Sensors, small tools, brackets, and lengths of conduit all have to be carried on a pipe that cannot be taken out of service, cannot be lifted, and has no free end over which a closed ring could be threaded. A clamp intended for that duty therefore has to open from the side, close around the pipe, and grip it firmly enough that the carried equipment keeps its position, while remaining removable so that the same clamp can be taken off and used again elsewhere.
2	
3	A clamp that opens from the side is split into parts, and the split is what makes the gripping problem difficult. Once the clamp body is divided, any drive element that runs around the body is divided with it. If the gripping surfaces of each part are driven separately, the fixed relationship between the two parts of the drive is given up: the two sides of the clamp advance by amounts that depend on how each side is operated, so the clamp tends to settle off center on the pipe, and the load is shared unevenly between the gripping surfaces. If the split body is instead pulled closed on the pipe, the closing force passes through the joint at the split and the pipe itself reacts the closing motion, so the grip depends on how nearly the bore of the clamp matches the outside diameter of the pipe, and a part dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter is needed, so that a different pipe size calls for a different part.
4	
5	Reusable clamping also has to deal with the force the operator applies. A hand lever gives the operator no measure of what has been done to the pipe. When the gripping elements have reached the pipe, further travel of the lever has to go somewhere, and in a rigid drive train it goes into whichever gripping element happens to touch first, so that one gripping surface is loaded far more than the others. Concentrated loading of a single gripping surface is undesirable, and the operator has no indication that it has occurred. An added instrument that responds to the position of the gripping elements reports the size of the pipe rather than the force in the grip.
6	
7	What has been lacking is a split clamp in which the drive that advances the gripping elements is itself coupled by the act of closing the clamp into a single element that moves as one ring, in which every gripping element is advanced from that one drive so that the gripping elements advance together over a range of pipe sizes, and in which the travel remaining in the operator's lever after the gripping elements have landed on the pipe is absorbed within the clamp and reported to the operator as a loading condition rather than as a dimension.
8

3	In one aspect, a split pipe clamp comprises a first frame half and a second frame half joined at a hinge end by a hinge and releasably joined at a latch end by a latch. In a closed condition the two frame halves define a frame having an annular guide and three radial guides. Three jaw carriages are each slidable radially in a respective one of the radial guides, and each jaw carriage carries a jaw pad that is pivotally mounted on the jaw carriage and has a concave bearing face directed inwardly of the frame. Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the segmented cam ring, each oblique slot being inclined to a radial direction of the frame so that rotation of the coupled ring through a stroke advances the three jaw carriages inwardly in synchronism. A wedge movable by the latch bears on a ring drive face of the segmented cam ring, so that movement of the latch rotates the coupled ring through the stroke, and a carriage return spring biases each jaw carriage outwardly so that releasing the latch retracts the jaws.

5	Because the coupled ring is a single kinematic element spanning both frame halves, the three jaw carriages are not driven independently. One latch motion, applied at one point on one frame half, is distributed by the coupled ring to every jaw carriage, and the jaw pads close on the pipe together. An indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of a latch housing when the force-limiting spring stack enters a predetermined compression range, giving the operator a mechanical report of clamp loading that is produced by the state of the spring stack and not by the diameter of the pipe.

1	The following description of embodiments refers to the accompanying drawings. The same reference numeral denotes the same part throughout. Terms of direction are used with respect to the frame of the clamp: the axis of the frame is the axis about which the frame is annular in the closed condition, "inward" and "radially inward" mean toward that axis, "outward" and "radially outward" mean away from it, and "circumferential" means about that axis. These terms describe relationships within the clamp and do not require the clamp to be used in any particular attitude.
2	
3	Overall arrangement
4	
5	FIG. 1 shows a split pipe clamp 100 closed around a pipe 90, with the latch 16 in the over-center position described below and the jaw pads 40 seated on the pipe 90. The clamp 100 has a first frame half 10 and a second frame half 12. Each of the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 is semicircular, and the two frame halves together surround the pipe 90. The first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are joined at one end, referred to as the hinge end, by a hinge 14, and are releasably joined at the other end, referred to as the latch end, by a releasable latch 16. The hinge 14 permits the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 to be swung apart far enough for the frame halves to be placed around the pipe 90 from the side. When the frame halves are brought together and the latch 16 is engaged, the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 define a frame that is annular about the axis of the frame.
6	
7	Three jaw carriages 30 are distributed around the frame in the closed condition, so that the three jaw carriages 30 approach the pipe 90 from three different directions. Each jaw carriage 30 moves radially with respect to the frame and carries at its inner end a jaw pad 40, which is described below in connection with FIG. 3. The jaw pads 40 carried at the inner ends of the three jaw carriages 30 bear on the pipe 90 when the clamp 100 is clamped. The clamp 100 does not require a part dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter, and the same clamp 100 serves pipes of different diameters within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.
8	
9	The frame may carry a mounting boss 70 outside the annular guide 18 described below, as shown in FIG. 5, which is a fragmentary view with parts shown in section on a plane containing the axis of the frame and corresponding in orientation to the plane of FIG. 3, that plane passing through the mounting boss 70. The mounting boss 70 supports equipment 80 that is to be held on the pipe 90 by the clamp 100. FIG. 5 shows the equipment 80 supported on the mounting boss 70, the equipment 80 being a sensor, a tool, or a conduit. The mounting boss 70 does not participate in the advance of the three jaw carriages 30 inwardly in synchronism. FIG. 5 also shows the annular guide 18 of the frame with the segmented cam ring 20 received in it, the mounting boss 70 standing outside the annular guide 18, no part of the mounting boss 70 reaching into the annular guide 18. The equipment 80 carried at the mounting boss 70 therefore lies outside the drive path by which the jaws are advanced. The mounting boss 70 is an optional feature of the clamp 100 and may be omitted.
10	
11	The segmented cam ring
12	
13	FIG. 2 shows the segmented cam ring 20, drawn removed from the frame, its segments being in the relative positions they occupy when coupled in the closed condition. The segmented cam ring 20 comprises a first cam ring segment 22 and a second cam ring segment 24. The first cam ring segment 22 is carried by the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 is carried by the second frame half 12, so that each frame half carries one segment of the ring and each segment travels with its own frame half when the clamp 100 is opened.
14	
15	The first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 meet at two places, one at the hinge end and one at the latch end. At the hinge end the two segments have complementary coupling faces 26, and at the latch end they have complementary coupling faces 28. The complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 are each shaped so that one segment can transmit circumferential force to the other through the joint. The faces are brought into engagement by the same motion that closes the frame halves: as the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are swung together about the hinge 14, the complementary coupling faces 26 close on one another at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces 28 close on one another at the latch end. FIG. 6 shows the joint at the latch end in the closed condition, the end of the first cam ring segment 22 held by the first frame half 10 and the end of the second cam ring segment 24 held by the second frame half 12, the two ends meeting at the complementary coupling faces 28.
16	
17	Coupling the segments in this way solves a problem created by splitting the clamp. Here the division of the ring is undone by the act of closing the clamp. In the closed condition the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 are coupled at both ends and rotate together in the annular guide as a coupled ring, and a circumferential input applied to either segment is carried around the whole ring. One input, applied at one point on one frame half, therefore reaches every jaw carriage 30 through a single kinematic element, and the relationship between the jaw carriages 30 is set by the geometry of the ring rather than by the way the clamp is operated. When the latch 16 is released and the frame halves are swung apart, the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 separate and each segment stays with its own frame half, so that the coupling is made and broken by the closing and opening of the frame halves.
18	
19	The annular guide 18 retains the first cam ring segment 22 on the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 on the second frame half 12, and permits circumferential movement of the coupled ring. Each segment is therefore held on its own frame half whether the clamp 100 is open or closed, and no separate operation is needed to place the ring in the frame when the frame halves are brought together.
20	
21	The segmented cam ring 20 has three oblique slots 34, one for each jaw carriage 30. Each oblique slot 34 is inclined to the radial direction of the frame at the circumferential position of that slot, so that rotation of the coupled ring produces inward travel of its jaw carriage 30, the three oblique slots 34 being arranged so that the three jaw carriages 30 travel inwardly in synchronism.
22	
23	The segmented cam ring 20 further has a ring drive face 36, shown in FIG. 2 at the latch end of the ring, against which the latch 16 acts through a wedge 52 as described below. The ring drive face 36 is presented at a position on the ring that the wedge 52 can reach, and it lies at an inclination to the direction in which the wedge 52 advances, so that advance of the wedge 52 moves the segmented cam ring 20 circumferentially.
24	
25	The jaw carriages
26	
27	FIG. 3 is a fragmentary sectional view through one jaw carriage 30, taken on line 3-3 of FIG. 1. The frame is formed with the annular guide 18, which receives the segmented cam ring 20 and holds it against radial movement while leaving it free to move circumferentially.
28

The follower 32 bears against the sides of the oblique slot 34.

31	The follower 32 is constrained in two ways at once. The radial guide 38 prevents the jaw carriage 30, and therefore the follower 32, from moving circumferentially, while the oblique slot 34 holds the follower 32 at a position along the slot, which is inclined to the radial direction, so that circumferential movement of the segmented cam ring 20 displaces the follower 32 radially. When the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the side of each oblique slot 34 bears on the corresponding follower 32 and drives it, and with it the jaw carriage 30, radially inward along the radial guide 38. Because all three followers 32 are engaged in oblique slots 34 of one coupled ring, the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism for as long as the ring turns. The jaw pads 40 therefore close on the pipe together.
32	
33	At its inner end each jaw carriage 30 carries a jaw pad 40. The jaw pad 40 is pivotally mounted on the jaw carriage 30 and has a concave bearing face directed inwardly of the frame. Because the jaw pad 40 is free to pivot on the jaw carriage 30, the concave bearing face aligns itself with the outer surface of the pipe as it lands. The same concave bearing face therefore seats on pipes of different diameters, and no part dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter is required.

The latch housing 58 presents a fixed edge referred to below in connection with the indicator pin 56. The wedge 52 is positioned so that its inclined face bears on the ring drive face 36 of the segmented cam ring 20.

In a first position, the latch 16 holds the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 closed around the pipe 90 but does not clamp it: the frame is captive on the pipe 90 and cannot fall away, while the segmented cam ring 20 has not yet advanced the jaw carriages 30. In a second, over-center position, the wedge 52 drives the segmented cam ring 20 and the pipe 90 is clamped. Movement of the latch handle 50 from the first position to the second position advances the wedge 52 against the ring drive face 36. The inclined face of the wedge 52 converts that advance into circumferential movement of the segmented cam ring 20, and the coupled ring turns through its limited stroke.

The jaw pads 40 land on the pipe 90 at some point in the stroke that depends on the diameter of the pipe 90, and the latch handle 50 has still to be carried into its over-center position. If the drive train from the latch handle 50 to the wedge 52 were rigid, that remaining travel would be taken up by whatever part of the assembly yielded first, in practice by driving one jaw farther into the pipe 90 than the others and loading it far more heavily. Additional travel of the latch handle 50 after all three jaw pads 40 have contacted the pipe 90 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 54 rather than forcing one jaw carriage 30 farther inward than the others.

As the force-limiting spring stack 54 compresses, the indicator pin 56 moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing 58, and the position of the indicator pin 56 with respect to that fixed edge shows the operator when the force-limiting spring stack 54 has entered a predetermined compression range. The indicator pin 56 therefore reports clamp loading mechanically, and what it reports is the state of the force-limiting spring stack 54. The indicator pin 56 is displaced by compression of the force-limiting spring stack 54 independently of a diameter of the pipe 90, and its position is not a measurement of that diameter.

The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 90 from the side and closes them about the hinge 14. The following description of embodiments refers to the accompanying drawings. The same reference numeral denotes the same part throughout. Terms of direction are used with respect to the frame of the clamp: the axis of the frame is the axis about which the frame is annular in the closed condition, "inward" and "radially inward" mean toward that axis, "outward" and "radially outward" mean away from it, and "circumferential" means about that axis. These terms describe relationships within the clamp and do not require the clamp to be used in any particular attitude.

Overall arrangement

FIG. 1 shows a split pipe clamp 100 closed around a pipe 90, with the latch 16 in the over-center position described below and the jaw pads 40 seated on the pipe 90. The clamp 100 has a first frame half 10 and a second frame half 12. Each of the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 is semicircular, and the two frame halves together surround the pipe 90. The first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are joined at one end, referred to as the hinge end, by a hinge 14, and are releasably joined at the other end, referred to as the latch end, by a releasable latch 16. The hinge 14 permits the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 to be swung apart far enough for the frame halves to be placed around the pipe 90 from the side. When the frame halves are brought together and the latch 16 is engaged, the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 define a frame that is annular about the axis of the frame.

Three jaw carriages 30 are distributed around the frame in the closed condition, so that the three jaw carriages 30 approach the pipe 90 from three different directions. Each jaw carriage 30 moves radially with respect to the frame and carries at its inner end a jaw pad 40, which is described below in connection with FIG. 3. The jaw pads 40 carried at the inner ends of the three jaw carriages 30 bear on the pipe 90 when the clamp 100 is clamped. The clamp 100 does not require a part dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter, and the same clamp 100 serves pipes of different diameters within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

The frame may carry a mounting boss 70 outside the annular guide 18 described below, as shown in FIG. 5, which is a fragmentary view with parts shown in section on a plane containing the axis of the frame and corresponding in orientation to the plane of FIG. 3, that plane passing through the mounting boss 70. The mounting boss 70 supports equipment 80 that is to be held on the pipe 90 by the clamp 100. FIG. 5 shows the equipment 80 supported on the mounting boss 70, the equipment 80 being a sensor, a tool, or a conduit. The mounting boss 70 does not participate in the advance of the three jaw carriages 30 inwardly in synchronism. FIG. 5 also shows the annular guide 18 of the frame with the segmented cam ring 20 received in it, the mounting boss 70 standing outside the annular guide 18, no part of the mounting boss 70 reaching into the annular guide 18. The equipment 80 carried at the mounting boss 70 therefore lies outside the drive path by which the jaws are advanced. The mounting boss 70 is an optional feature of the clamp 100 and may be omitted.

The segmented cam ring

FIG. 2 shows the segmented cam ring 20, drawn removed from the frame, its segments being in the relative positions they occupy when coupled in the closed condition. The segmented cam ring 20 comprises a first cam ring segment 22 and a second cam ring segment 24. The first cam ring segment 22 is carried by the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 is carried by the second frame half 12, so that each frame half carries one segment of the ring and each segment travels with its own frame half when the clamp 100 is opened.

The first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 meet at two places, one at the hinge end and one at the latch end. At the hinge end the two segments have complementary coupling faces 26, and at the latch end they have complementary coupling faces 28. The complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 are each shaped so that one segment can transmit circumferential force to the other through the joint. The faces are brought into engagement by the same motion that closes the frame halves: as the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are swung together about the hinge 14, the complementary coupling faces 26 close on one another at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces 28 close on one another at the latch end. FIG. 6 shows the joint at the latch end in the closed condition, the end of the first cam ring segment 22 held by the first frame half 10 and the end of the second cam ring segment 24 held by the second frame half 12, the two ends meeting at the complementary coupling faces 28.

Coupling the segments in this way solves a problem created by splitting the clamp. Here the division of the ring is undone by the act of closing the clamp. In the closed condition the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 are coupled at both ends and rotate together in the annular guide as a coupled ring, and a circumferential input applied to either segment is carried around the whole ring. One input, applied at one point on one frame half, therefore reaches every jaw carriage 30 through a single kinematic element, and the relationship between the jaw carriages 30 is set by the geometry of the ring rather than by the way the clamp is operated. When the latch 16 is released and the frame halves are swung apart, the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 separate and each segment stays with its own frame half, so that the coupling is made and broken by the closing and opening of the frame halves.

The annular guide 18 retains the first cam ring segment 22 on the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 on the second frame half 12, and permits circumferential movement of the coupled ring. Each segment is therefore held on its own frame half whether the clamp 100 is open or closed, and no separate operation is needed to place the ring in the frame when the frame halves are brought together.

The segmented cam ring 20 has three oblique slots 34, one for each jaw carriage 30. Each oblique slot 34 is inclined to the radial direction of the frame at the circumferential position of that slot, so that rotation of the coupled ring produces inward travel of its jaw carriage 30, the three oblique slots 34 being arranged so that the three jaw carriages 30 travel inwardly in synchronism.

The segmented cam ring 20 further has a ring drive face 36, shown in FIG. 2 at the latch end of the ring, against which the latch 16 acts through a wedge 52 as described below. The ring drive face 36 is presented at a position on the ring that the wedge 52 can reach, and it lies at an inclination to the direction in which the wedge 52 advances, so that advance of the wedge 52 moves the segmented cam ring 20 circumferentially.

The jaw carriages

FIG. 3 is a fragmentary sectional view through one jaw carriage 30, taken on line 3-3 of FIG. 1. The frame is formed with the annular guide 18, which receives the segmented cam ring 20 and holds it against radial movement while leaving it free to move circumferentially.

The frame is further formed with a radial guide 38 at the position of each jaw carriage 30, so that the frame in the closed condition has the annular guide 18 and three radial guides 38. Each jaw carriage 30 is received in a respective one of the three radial guides 38 and is constrained by the radial guide 38 to move radially with respect to the frame. Each jaw carriage 30 carries a follower 32 that projects from the jaw carriage 30 into a respective one of the oblique slots 34 of the segmented cam ring 20. The follower 32 bears against the sides of the oblique slot 34.

The follower 32 is constrained in two ways at once. The radial guide 38 prevents the jaw carriage 30, and therefore the follower 32, from moving circumferentially, while the oblique slot 34 holds the follower 32 at a position along the slot, which is inclined to the radial direction, so that circumferential movement of the segmented cam ring 20 displaces the follower 32 radially. When the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the side of each oblique slot 34 bears on the corresponding follower 32 and drives it, and with it the jaw carriage 30, radially inward along the radial guide 38. Because all three followers 32 are engaged in oblique slots 34 of one coupled ring, the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism for as long as the ring turns. The jaw pads 40 therefore close on the pipe together.

At its inner end each jaw carriage 30 carries a jaw pad 40. The jaw pad 40 is pivotally mounted on the jaw carriage 30 and has a concave bearing face directed inwardly of the frame. Because the jaw pad 40 is free to pivot on the jaw carriage 30, the concave bearing face aligns itself with the outer surface of the pipe as it lands. The same concave bearing face therefore seats on pipes of different diameters, and no part dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter is required.

A carriage return spring 44 acts on each jaw carriage 30 so as to urge that jaw carriage 30 radially outward. When the latch 16 is released and the drive from the latch to the ring drive face 36 is removed, the carriage return springs 44 push the jaw carriages 30 outward and the jaw pads 40 are retracted from the pipe, and the clamp 100 is left with its jaw carriages 30 retracted and ready for the next installation. Retraction of the jaw carriages 30 clears the jaw pads 40 from the pipe before the frame halves are swung apart.

The latch and the force-limiting drive train

The latch 16 comprises a latch housing 58 at the latch end, a latch handle 50, and a force-limiting spring stack 54 in a drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52, the wedge 52 being movable by the latch 16. The latch housing 58 presents a fixed edge referred to below in connection with the indicator pin 56. The wedge 52 is positioned so that its inclined face bears on the ring drive face 36 of the segmented cam ring 20.

FIG. 4 is an enlarged fragmentary view of the latch end, with parts shown in section, and shows the latch housing 58, the latch handle 50, the wedge 52, the force-limiting spring stack 54 and the indicator pin 56 in their relation to the first cam ring segment 22, the second cam ring segment 24 and the ring drive face 36.

The latch 16 has two engaged positions. In a first position, the latch 16 holds the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 closed around the pipe 90 but does not clamp it: the frame is captive on the pipe 90 and cannot fall away, while the segmented cam ring 20 has not yet advanced the jaw carriages 30. In a second, over-center position, the wedge 52 drives the segmented cam ring 20 and the pipe 90 is clamped. Movement of the latch handle 50 from the first position to the second position advances the wedge 52 against the ring drive face 36. The inclined face of the wedge 52 converts that advance into circumferential movement of the segmented cam ring 20, and the coupled ring turns through its limited stroke.

The force-limiting spring stack 54 answers the problem of what becomes of the operator's remaining handle travel. The jaw pads 40 land on the pipe 90 at some point in the stroke that depends on the diameter of the pipe 90, and the latch handle 50 has still to be carried into its over-center position. If the drive train from the latch handle 50 to the wedge 52 were rigid, that remaining travel would be taken up by whatever part of the assembly yielded first, in practice by driving one jaw farther into the pipe 90 than the others and loading it far more heavily. Additional travel of the latch handle 50 after all three jaw pads 40 have contacted the pipe 90 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 54 rather than forcing one jaw carriage 30 farther inward than the others.

The indicator pin 56 is coupled to the force-limiting spring stack 54 and projects from the latch housing 58. As the force-limiting spring stack 54 compresses, the indicator pin 56 moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing 58, and the position of the indicator pin 56 with respect to that fixed edge shows the operator when the force-limiting spring stack 54 has entered a predetermined compression range. The indicator pin 56 therefore reports clamp loading mechanically, and what it reports is the state of the force-limiting spring stack 54. The indicator pin 56 is displaced by compression of the force-limiting spring stack 54 independently of a diameter of the pipe 90, and its position is not a measurement of that diameter.

Operation

To install the clamp 100 on a pipe 90, the operator opens the latch 16 and swings the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 apart about the hinge 14. The first cam ring segment 22 stays with the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 stays with the second frame half 12, and the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 are separated. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 90 from the side and closes them about the hinge 14. Closing the frame halves brings the complementary coupling faces 26 into engagement at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces 28 into engagement at the latch end, coupling the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 into the coupled ring within the annular guide 18.

The operator then moves the latch 16 to its first position, in which the frame is held around the pipe 90 without clamping. The operator moves the latch handle 50 to the second, over-center position. The wedge 52 is driven against the ring drive face 36, the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the sides of the three oblique slots 34 drive the three followers 32, and the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism until the pivoting jaw pads 40 seat on the pipe 90. The remaining travel of the latch handle 50 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 54, and the operator watches the indicator pin 56 move relative to the fixed edge of the latch housing 58 and so sees that the force-limiting spring stack 54 has entered the predetermined compression range. The latch 16 is left in the over-center position and the clamp 100 is loaded on the pipe 90.

To remove the clamp 100, the operator releases the latch 16. The latch handle 50 comes back over center, the wedge 52 retreats from the ring drive face 36, and the force-limiting spring stack 54 is unloaded. The carriage return springs 44 then push the jaw carriages 30 radially outward, so that the jaw pads 40 lift from the pipe 90. Only then are the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 swung apart about the hinge 14 and the clamp 100 taken off the pipe 90. The clamp 100 may be installed again on the same pipe or on a pipe of a different diameter within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

Features described above in connection with one embodiment may be combined with features described in connection with another, except where the context makes the combination impossible. The embodiments described are illustrative of the disclosed clamp and are not exhaustive of it, and the scope of protection is defined by the claims that follow rather than by any particular embodiment described here.

Enlarged fragmentary detail of the latch-end joint of the clamp, viewed along the frame axis from the same side as FIG. 1, with the wall of the frame nearest the viewer broken away over the region shown, the frame and the two cam ring segments being shown in section at the break. Here the circumferential direction of the frame runs vertically and radially outward is toward the right. The view is confined to the two frame ends at this joint and the two segment ends. Cut material carries section hatching; the upper frame body, the lower frame body and each of the two cam ring segments carry hatching at a slant different from that of every other cut element it touches, so the parting line and the contact between the segment end faces stay distinct. Black line work on white, well inside the drawing area. Shown schematically: the extent of the region, the proportions of the bodies, the form of the meeting surfaces, and the extent of the break at each body's radially outer side.

Two hatched bodies stand one above the other, filling the upper and lower parts of the view, with a parting line between them running the full width of the view. The upper body is the latch end of the first frame half 10 and the lower body is the latch end of the second frame half 12. Each body is bounded on the left by an upright edge, on the right by an irregular break line, and toward the parting line by a straight horizontal end face.

The annular guide 18 of each frame half appears as a channel opening toward the parting line, one in the upper body opening downward and one in the lower body opening upward. Each channel is set back from the left edge of its body, so a band of hatched frame material stands between the channel and that edge. In the upper body a further band of hatched frame material stands between the channel and the break line at its right. In the lower body also a band of hatched frame material stands between the channel and the break line at its right.

A solid block lies in each channel and reaches along it to the end face of its body without passing beyond it. The block in the upper body is the first cam ring segment 22 and the block in the lower body is the second cam ring segment 24. The two blocks are of the same width and stand in line.

At the parting line the lower end face of the first cam ring segment 22 and the upper end face of the second cam ring segment 24 lie against one another where they meet, so that one segment can transmit circumferential force to the other; the form of those surfaces and the extent of their engagement are shown schematically. Those surfaces in contact are the complementary coupling faces at the latch end 28.

## Numerals shown on this figure

- 10 first frame half: target the hatched band between the channel of the upper body and its left edge.
- 12 second frame half: target the hatched band between the channel of the lower body and its left edge.
- 18 annular guide: target the surface of the channel wall in the upper body on the radially outer side of the block that lies in the channel.
- 22 first cam ring segment: target the hatching inside the block in the upper body, away from the parting line.
- 24 second cam ring segment: target the hatching inside the block in the lower body, away from the parting line.
- 28 complementary coupling faces at the latch end: target the horizontal contact between the end faces of the two blocks at the parting line.

Ledger scope: I traced every claim limitation (claims 1-15), every numeral in draft/numerals.md (10-100), and every structure, relationship, result, position, connection, condition and variant in draft/04 through draft/10 and in figures/FIG-1..FIG-6 to the inventor text. The disclosure and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md are identical in substance, so both were used as one authority.

Supported and clean (no findings): the split frame with two semicircular halves, hinge at one end, releasable latch at the other; three radial jaw carriages in radial guides; pivoting concave jaw pads and diameter-independent seating; the segmented cam ring retained in an annular guide with one segment per frame half; complementary coupling faces at the hinge end and at the latch end engaged by closing the frame; the coupled ring rotating as one element; three followers in three oblique slots inclined to the radial direction producing synchronized inward travel; the wedge driven by the latch against a ring drive face; the limited stroke; carriage return springs biasing each carriage outward; the two latch positions including the over-center position; the force-limiting spring stack between latch handle and wedge absorbing remaining handle travel; the indicator pin reading against a fixed edge of the latch housing at a predetermined compression range and reporting loading rather than diameter; the install and removal sequence; and the optional mounting boss outside the annular guide carrying a sensor, tool or conduit and not participating in synchronization. Claims 1-15 are all traceable on these facts, including dependent limitations (claims 3, 5, 6, 7, 9) and the assembly claim 10 and method claims 13-15. Background prior-art characterizations were not traced, as instructed. Title, "Not applicable" cross-reference, and "Not applicable" government-support statement match input/brief.md.

Internal-consistency checks performed and passed: every numeral in numerals.md is used in draft/08 and in at least one figure brief, and no numeral carries two meanings; every numeral listed in each figure brief appears in the corresponding description passage; the only section designation, line 3-3, is used identically in figures/FIG-1.md, figures/FIG-3.md, draft/07-drawings.md and draft/08-detailed-description.md, with arrow direction consistent with FIG. 3's stated axial orientation; the FIG. 4 "opposite side" and FIG. 6 "same side" viewing statements are geometrically consistent with FIG. 1's placement of the first frame half above and the latch at the right (first segment 22 appears at the right in FIG. 4 and at the top in FIG. 6, as required); the annular guide's axial opening direction is consistent across FIG. 3, FIG. 5 and FIG. 6 (the broken-away near wall in FIG. 6 is the closed wall of FIG. 3); claims, summary, abstract and description use the same terms ("complementary coupling faces at the hinge end / at the latch end", "ring drive face", "coupled ring", "force-limiting spring stack"); the abstract is 142 words; and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in the application text. The description text adds no shape-justifying language such as "by way of example" or "any closed outline".

Findings: five items, all confined to the figure briefs; none require a change to the application text, because draft/08 keeps the affected geometry generic ("presented at a position on the ring that the wedge 52 can reach", "at an inclination to the direction in which the wedge 52 advances"). Two are critical. First, figures/FIG-4.md asserts an opening in the frame wall through which the wedge reaches the ring drive face; no opening, window or break in the frame is disclosed anywhere in the source. Second, the ring drive face - a functional cam/ramp surface - is given a radial position (on the radially outer boundary of the ring), a circumferential position (on the arc of the second cam ring segment 24 near the latch joint), and a mating wedge that advances radially inward onto it. The source says only that the latch "drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring"; it never says which segment carries the face, on which side of the ring it lies, or from which direction the wedge approaches. Under the functional-surface rule these radial and circumferential end positions and the contact topology are substantive even though the brief labels them schematic. The remaining three are a pivot joint between the latch handle and the latch housing plus a handle opening between the housing walls (major), the oblique slot depicted as passing clear through the cam ring from face to face (minor depth assertion, where the source says only that the follower is "received in" the slot), and hinge knuckle blocks reaching from each frame end with the hinge stated to lie wholly within the width of the frame body (minor). Each fix strips the untraced relationship while leaving a minimally specific generic depiction of the part the inventor did disclose; none adds a speculative shape or optional embodiment to the application text.

findings.title: FIG. 4 brief creates an undisclosed opening in the frame wall at the wedge
findings.where: figures/FIG-4.md, paragraph beginning "Between the latch housing 58 and the left band..."
findings.detail: The brief asserts that the frame wall is open over the region where the wedge meets the ring drive face. An aperture, window or break in the frame wall is a structural feature of the frame and a force path, not a shape convention. The disclosure never mentions any opening in the frame; it says only that the wedge is driven against a drive face of the cam ring. Labelling the extent of the opening "schematic" does not cure the assertion that the opening exists. The application text does not recite this opening, so the fix is confined to the figure brief.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-4.md): "Between the latch housing 58 and the left band the frame wall is open over the short region in which the wedge 52 meets the ring drive face 36, the extent of that opening being shown schematically." Nearest source passage (input/disclosure.md; identical USER text in input/conversation.md): "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke." No affirmative passage in the disclosure or in any USER message discloses an opening, window, port or break in the frame wall.
findings.fix: Delete that sentence from figures/FIG-4.md. In its place, and consistent with figures/FIG-6.md (where the annular guide of each frame half opens at the frame end face toward the parting line), have the cavity of the latch housing 58 open downward toward the parting line between the two frame ends, where the end region of the cam ring segment is exposed, and show the wedge 52 bearing on the ring drive face 36 there. Do not describe any opening, window or break in the frame wall.

findings.title: Ring drive face given an undisclosed radial side, segment and wedge approach direction
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md, paragraph beginning "The ring drive face 36 is a short straight flat..."; figures/FIG-4.md, paragraphs beginning "Between the latch housing 58..." and "Above the parting line a hatched enclosure..."
findings.detail: The ring drive face is a functional cam/ramp surface. The briefs place it on the radially outer boundary of the ring, attribute it to the second cam ring segment 24 in the arc near the latch joint, and pair it with a wedge that descends radially inward from a housing cavity onto it. The source discloses the drive face and the wedge, but nothing about which segment carries the face, which radial side of the ring it lies on, or the direction from which the wedge advances. Radial and circumferential end positions and contact topology of a functional face are substantive even where the brief labels them schematic. Only the generic fact that the face is inclined so that wedge advance turns the ring is supported, and that generic statement is what the description already carries.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-2.md): "The ring drive face 36 is a short straight flat on the outer boundary of the second cam ring segment 24, in the arc near the right joint, lying at an inclination to the circular outer boundary so that a wedge advancing on it can move the ring circumferentially." Candidate (figures/FIG-4.md): "In that region the ring drive face 36 is one straight surface lying at an inclination to the radially outer side of the band"; "a cavity opening downward over the ring drive face 36. A block, the wedge 52, lies in that cavity, its lower face inclined to bear on the ring drive face 36". Nearest source passage: "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke." No affirmative passage assigns the drive face to either segment, to the outer periphery, or specifies the wedge's direction of advance. Supporting text that does trace: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "it lies at an inclination to the direction in which the wedge 52 advances, so that advance of the wedge 52 moves the segmented cam ring 20 circumferentially."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md, replace the quoted sentence with: "The ring drive face 36 is a short plain straight face of the segmented cam ring 20 in the region of the right joint, drawn inclined so that a wedge bearing on it can move the ring circumferentially; which segment carries it, its radial side, its slant and its extent are not specified." In figures/FIG-4.md, delete "lying at an inclination to the radially outer side of the band" and "its lower face inclined", and state instead that the wedge 52 bears on the ring drive face 36 through a plain inclined contact so that advance of the wedge 52 moves the band circumferentially, without stating the radial side of the face, which segment carries it, or the direction in which the wedge advances. Leave draft/08-detailed-description.md unchanged, as its wording is already generic and supported.

findings.title: FIG. 4 brief adds an undisclosed pivot joint between latch handle and latch housing, and an undisclosed opening between housing walls
findings.where: figures/FIG-4.md, paragraph beginning "The latch handle 50 is pivoted to the latch housing 58..."
findings.detail: The brief specifies a joint (a pivot at a stated location on the housing cavity) and a second aperture (an opening between the top and right housing walls through which the handle passes). A joint and its location, and an aperture in a part, are connections and topology that convey technical substance; they are not covered by the schematic-housing convention. The source discloses a latch handle, a latch housing with a fixed edge, and an over-center latch position, but never says how the handle is mounted or that it passes through the housing wall. The application text does not recite the pivot or the opening, so the fix is confined to the figure brief.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-4.md): "The latch handle 50 is pivoted to the latch housing 58 at a small circle at the upper right of the cavity and runs up and to the right through an opening between the top and right walls, leaning past upright, the over-center position, as a straight bar of even width." Nearest source passages: "A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge"; "The latch has a first position that holds the frame halves around the pipe without clamping and a second over-center position that drives the cam ring and clamps the pipe." No affirmative passage describes the mounting of the handle or an opening in the latch housing.
findings.fix: Replace the quoted sentence in figures/FIG-4.md with: "The latch handle 50 is a plain straight bar of even width extending outward from the latch housing 58 and leaning past upright, the over-center position. Its mounting is not depicted; no pivot joint and no opening in the housing walls is shown." Delete the corresponding item "the attitude, outline and mounting of the latch handle 50" from the schematic list only insofar as it refers to the mounting.

findings.title: FIG. 3 brief states the oblique slot passes clear through the cam ring
findings.where: figures/FIG-3.md, paragraph beginning "A hatched block is received in the groove..."
findings.detail: The brief asserts that the oblique slot is an opening running from one face of the cam ring to the other. For a functional slot, a statement of depth or breakout is substantive even when labelled schematic. The source says only that the follower is "received in" the slot, which supports a slot that receives the follower but not one that breaks out at the far face.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-3.md): "One short rectangular opening passes through that block from its left face to its right face; apart from that opening the block is solid and hatched throughout. That opening is the oblique slot 34, its position in the block shown schematically." Nearest source passage: "Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring." No affirmative passage states that the slot passes through the ring.
findings.fix: Replace with: "One short rectangular opening is formed in the left face of that block, sized to receive the follower 32; apart from that opening the block is solid and hatched throughout. That opening is the oblique slot 34, its position in the block shown schematically, and it is not shown breaking out at the right face." No change is needed in figures/FIG-2.md, whose wording ("the face of the ring is flat and unbroken except where the three slots open in it") is already neutral.

findings.title: FIG. 1 brief adds undisclosed hinge knuckle structure and a radial containment statement
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md, paragraph beginning "At the left joint is the hinge 14..."
findings.detail: Beyond placing the disclosed hinge at the joint, the brief adds a short block reaching to the hinge from each frame end (knuckle structure and a connection to each frame end) and asserts that the whole hinge lies within the width of the frame body (a radial containment relationship for a functional joint). Neither is disclosed. Placing a small circle on the joint line is the minimally specific depiction the disclosed hinge requires; the added structure and containment statement are not.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-1.md): "At the left joint is the hinge 14, shown schematically as a small circle on that joint line between the inner circle and the outer circle, with a short block reaching to it from each frame end, the whole hinge 14 lying within the width of the frame body." Nearest source passage: "a first semicircular frame half and a second semicircular frame half joined by a hinge at one end and a releasable latch at the other end." No affirmative passage describes hinge knuckles, blocks at the frame ends, or the radial extent of the hinge relative to the frame body.
findings.fix: Replace with: "At the left joint is the hinge 14, shown schematically as a small circle on that joint line between the inner circle and the outer circle." Delete the clauses "with a short block reaching to it from each frame end" and "the whole hinge 14 lying within the width of the frame body".

Findings: five items, all confined to the figure briefs; none require a change to the application text, because draft/08 keeps the affected geometry generic ("presented at a position on the ring that the wedge 52 can reach", "at an inclination to the direction in which the wedge 52 advances"). Two are critical. First, figures/FIG-4.md asserts an opening in the frame wall through which the wedge reaches the ring drive face; no opening, window or break in the frame is disclosed anywhere in the source. Second, the ring drive face - a functional cam/ramp surface - is given a radial position (on the radially outer boundary of the ring), a circumferential position (on the arc of the second cam ring segment 24 near the latch joint), and a mating wedge that advances radially inward onto it. The source says only that the latch "drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring"; it never says which segment carries the face, on which side of the ring it lies, or from which direction the wedge approaches. findings.title: Ring drive face given an undisclosed radial side, segment and wedge approach direction

findings.detail: The ring drive face is a functional cam/ramp surface. The briefs place it on the radially outer boundary of the ring, attribute it to the second cam ring segment 24 in the arc near the latch joint, and pair it with a wedge that descends radially inward from a housing cavity onto it. The source discloses the drive face and the wedge, but nothing about which segment carries the face, which radial side of the ring it lies on, or the direction from which the wedge advances. Radial and circumferential end positions and contact topology of a functional face are substantive even where the brief labels them schematic. Only the generic fact that the face is inclined so that wedge advance turns the ring is supported, and that generic statement is what the description already carries.
